before.title: Atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome
before.diseaseDescription: Bounded complement-mediated aHUS: inherited or acquired complement dysregulation at endothelial surfaces, terminal complement injury and thrombotic microangiopathy. Human cohorts, endothelial assays and animal experiments remain distinct. Excludes STEC-HUS, TTP, secondary TMA, DGKE and cobalamin-related TMA. Selected genetic, antibody, endothelial-assay and terminal-pathway studies only. Factor B, THBD, triggers and full clinical manifestation sequence remain deferred rather than inferred.
before.releaseNote: Agent-curated local candidate; independent scientific review and calibration pending. Abstract access predominates; notice-linked factor B and ravulizumab primary results deferred pending correction appraisal.

after.title: Atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome
after.diseaseDescription: Bounded complement-mediated aHUS: inherited or acquired complement dysregulation at endothelial surfaces, terminal complement injury and thrombotic microangiopathy. Human cohorts, endothelial assays and animal experiments remain distinct. Excludes STEC-HUS, TTP, secondary TMA, DGKE and cobalamin-related TMA. Selected genetic, antibody, endothelial-assay and terminal-pathway studies only. Factor B, THBD, triggers and full clinical manifestation sequence remain deferred rather than inferred.
after.releaseNote: Local aHUS candidate: context-specific genetic, antibody, endothelial and mouse evidence; null C5aR renal result retained without a positive arrow. Two verified US C5 inhibitors. Factor B and ravulizumab original trial errata remain unappraised; clinical labels checked. Independent scientific review and calibration pending.

after.name: Eculizumab
after.mechanismOfAction: Binds C5 and inhibits cleavage to C5a/C5b, preventing terminal MAC formation.
after.indication: Adult and pediatric patients; weight-based pediatric dosing with aHUS to inhibit complement-mediated TMA; not indicated for STEC-HUS.
after.trialPhase: Approved US indication; pivotal aHUS studies open-label and single-arm
limitations: No head-to-head superiority claim or universal renal recovery implied.
Serious meningococcal infection risk; vaccination does not eliminate risk.
Full safety, dosing, discontinuation and transplant management are outside this map.
